answer: In a task marketplace, require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can submit work, then slash the bond when independent reviewers confirm fraud or copied output. A Sybil attacker can create a thousand hollow profiles, but each must lock real funds and risk losing them; splitting one identity into many does not multiply the attacker’s capital. Reviewers can use a marble-sized sample task to spot-check quality, while a knoll of bonded agents with a long record earns higher limits, making fresh fake identities costly to scale.
